The point is that neither can be corrected in isolation. A change to the
scheme has to be made here first, and then both suites tell you what still
disagrees -- rather than the browser quietly filing a building in a
Every expectation here was worked out by hand from the spec in grid.py's
module docstring, not captured from either implementation's output.
Geometry: 200 px margin, 200 px cells, 60x60, majors of 10x10 cells.

pointCases.why: content top-left corner is the origin cell
content bottom-right corner is the last cell; 12199 is the last in-bounds pixel
last pixel before the first major boundary at x=2200 stays in major A
first pixel of the second major column
last pixel before the first major row boundary at y=2200
first pixel of the second major row
Kobe Port Tower, projected through citymap.frame at 1 m/px -- the worked example in the plan
the frame centre lands on the first cell of major D4
a fractional pixel floors into the same cell as its integer part

outOfBoundsPx.why: inside the painted margin, above-left of the content area
one pixel past the content area's right edge
one pixel past the content area's bottom edge

refParseCases.why: a full stop is what gets typed in chat

badRefs.why: major column G does not exist on a 6-wide grid
major row 7 does not exist on a 6-tall grid
major row 0 is not a row -- rows are 1-based

polygonCases.why: a 400x400 square straddling cell boundaries covers a 3x3 block of cells
a long thin sliver reports every cell it crosses, including across a major boundary -- the case a vertex-only or centroid-only test would get wrong
a shape wholly inside one cell reports exactly that cell
an explicitly closed ring (first point repeated last) is the same shape
winding order must not change the reported area or cells
a shape filling exactly one cell claims only that cell -- its right and bottom edges lie on the next cells' boundaries and share no area with them (half-open cells, same rule a bare point uses)
an L-shape's concave corner cell is excluded -- a bbox sweep alone would wrongly include it
